sentences.en: What are we looking at right now?
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到的是什么？

sentences.en: Wow, okay, so what are we looking at I think is a very strange contraption.
sentences.zh: 哇，好吧，我觉得我们看到的这个装置非常奇怪。

sentences.en: It doesn't really look like a clock, which is why it's so unique.
sentences.zh: 它看起来不太像钟表，这就是它独特的地方。

sentences.en: I have to say it looks extremely steampunk.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说它看起来非常有蒸汽朋克风格。

sentences.en: Like it could be in the Will Smith vehicle wild, wild weSt.
sentences.zh: 就像威尔·史密斯主演的《飙风战警》里会出现的东西。

sentences.en: Emily showed me Harrison's sea clock, which is on display at the Royal Observatory in Greenwich.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽带我看了哈里森的航海钟，它现在陈列在格林威治皇家天文台。

sentences.en: What I looked at with Emily was actually the inner workings of the clock because sometime over the years, the wooden case around it disappeared.
sentences.zh: 我和艾米丽看的是钟表的内部结构，因为多年来，它外面的木壳已经不见了。

sentences.en: The clock is made of gleaming brass with four small dials arranged on its face and an intricate system of tiny gears, springs and bars behind that.
sentences.zh: 这款钟表由闪亮的黄铜制成，表盘上排列着四个小表盘，后面是一套错综复杂的微型齿轮、弹簧和杠杆系统。

sentences.en: It weighs a hefty 75 pounds.
sentences.zh: 它重达75磅。

sentences.en: It's about the size of, what would you say?
sentences.zh: 它的大小大概是，你怎么形容呢？

sentences.en: I always say it might just, you might get away with it as cabin luggage.
sentences.zh: 我总说它可能，你或许能把它当作随身行李带上飞机。

sentences.en: You could, yeah, maybe.
sentences.zh: 是啊，或许可以。

sentences.en: Not with some airlines, but with a standard airline, you might get away carrying it.
sentences.zh: 有些航空公司不行，但普通航空公司的话，你可能可以带上它。

sentences.en: After Harrison finished H1 in 1735, he got it in front of England's premier research institute, the Royal Society.
sentences.zh: 1735年哈里森完成H1后，他把它带到了英国顶尖的研究机构——皇家学会。

sentences.en: This was a big moment for Harrison.
sentences.zh: 这对哈里森来说是一个重要的时刻。

sentences.en: A good review from the Society might put his invention in front of the judges of the Longitude Act.
sentences.zh: 如果能得到学会的好评，他的发明或许就能呈现在经度法案的评委面前。

sentences.en: While the Society was impressed with Harrison's clock, they were also pretty hesitant to trust that his idea would work.
sentences.zh: 虽然学会对哈里森的钟表印象深刻，但他们对他的想法能否奏效也相当怀疑。

sentences.en: Because why would they?
sentences.zh: 因为他们为什么要相信呢？

sentences.en: You know, he's just a guy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他只是个普通人。

sentences.en: He's doing all this in his home.
sentences.zh: 他是在自己家里完成这一切的。

sentences.en: At this point, Harrison was just a clockmaker with no scientific background.
sentences.zh: 当时，哈里森只是个没有科学背景的钟表匠。

sentences.en: So having some skepticism about the whole thing, the Society decided to give H1 a preliminary teSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，出于对整件事的怀疑，学会决定给H1做一个初步测试。

sentences.en: A test teSt.
sentences.zh: 一次试运行测试。

sentences.en: Not to the West Indies, but to Lisbon.
sentences.zh: 不是去西印度群岛，而是去里斯本。

sentences.en: They agreed to put it on a boat, but they just sent it to Portugal.
sentences.zh: 他们同意把它装上船，但只是把它送到了葡萄牙。

sentences.en: So not making the huge transatlantic voyage.
sentences.zh: 所以并没有进行跨大西洋的远航。

sentences.en: Harrison apparently got extremely seasick on the trip.
sentences.zh: 据说哈里森在这次旅途中晕船晕得非常厉害。

sentences.en: Like seasick enough that we are still talking about it 290 years later.
sentences.zh: 晕到我们290年后还在谈论这件事。

sentences.en: But H1 performed marvelously.
sentences.zh: 但H1的表现非常出色。

sentences.en: In fact, when the HMS Orford was on its way back to Britain, the ship's sailing master had them on course to pass a landmark just south of Dartmouth.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当“奥福德号”军舰返回英国时，船上的航海长根据航线本应经过达特茅斯以南的一个地标。

sentences.en: But Harrison, using H1, sounded the alarm.
sentences.zh: 但哈里森利用H1发出了警报。

sentences.en: He was able to pinpoint the ship's location as 60 miles off course to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他能够精确指出船只的位置偏离了航线，向西偏了60英里。

sentences.en: Harrison's timekeeper was able to correct the ship's longitude.
sentences.zh: 哈里森的计时器成功纠正了船只的经度。

sentences.en: Wow, that was a magic trick.
sentences.zh: 哇，那简直是魔术。

sentences.en: That was just, how did you do that?
sentences.zh: 那简直是，你是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: And how he had done it was with that clock.
sentences.zh: 而他做到这一切全靠那台钟表。

sentences.en: And the whole crew of the ship he was on, they're all ready to stand up for him.
sentences.zh: 他所在的整艘船的船员都准备为他站台。

sentences.en: He's not a crank.
sentences.zh: 他不是个怪人。

sentences.en: It's not what everybody was expecting.
sentences.zh: 这并不是大家所预期的那样。

sentences.en: But he's not a crank.
sentences.zh: 但他不是个怪人。

sentences.en: He's got something.
sentences.zh: 他确实有两把刷子。

sentences.en: So with the blessing of the Royal Society,
sentences.zh: 所以，在皇家学会的支持下，

sentences.en: all eight members of the official Board of Longitude assembled to hear about the successful Portugal trial and to judge Harrison's sea clock.
sentences.zh: 经度委员会的全部八名成员齐聚一堂，听取了葡萄牙试航成功的报告，并对哈里森的航海钟进行了评审。

sentences.en: And Harrison is there with his clock.
sentences.zh: 哈里森带着他的钟表出席了。

sentences.en: And what does he do?
sentences.zh: 结果他做了什么？

sentences.en: He says, I don't think it's really good enough yet.
sentences.zh: 他说，我觉得它还不够好。

sentences.en: He didn't want that big trial?
sentences.zh: 他不想进行那次大试航吗？

sentences.en: No, not yet.
sentences.zh: 不，还不是时候。

sentences.en: Harrison could have asked for his H1C clock to go on a trial to the West Indies.
sentences.zh: 哈里森本可以要求他的H1C钟表去西印度群岛进行试航。

sentences.en: And it's likely the board would have given it to him.
sentences.zh: 委员会很可能会答应他。

sentences.en: He could have tried for the prize.
sentences.zh: 他本可以去争取那个奖金。

sentences.en: But he didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 但他没有这样做。

sentences.en: What he did do was solidify his place as the absolute worst venture capitalist in the history of the world.
sentences.zh: 他所做的是巩固了自己作为世界历史上最糟糕的风险投资人的地位。

sentences.en: Harrison was so obsessed with getting his invention precisely, exactly, perfectly right,
sentences.zh: 哈里森太执着于让他的发明变得精准、确切、完美无缺，

sentences.en: that he showed up in a room full of people practically begging to give him a big pile of money, and he pointed out the problems with his own design.
sentences.zh: 以至于他出现在一屋子几乎求着给他一大笔钱的人面前时，却指出了自己设计中的问题。

sentences.en: Harrison, he was apparently the only person in the room to say anything negative about his work.
sentences.zh: 哈里森显然是房间里唯一一个对自己的作品说负面评价的人。

sentences.en: And so, like the terrible entrepreneur he was, Harrison went back to the drawing board.
sentences.zh: 于是，就像个糟糕的创业者一样，哈里森又回到了绘图板前。

sentences.en: So, H1, maybe we'd call that beta.
sentences.zh: 所以，H1，或许我们可以称之为测试版。

sentences.en: It proves the principle.
sentences.zh: 它证明了原理。

sentences.en: A clock on a boat will work.
sentences.zh: 船上的钟表是可以工作的。

sentences.en: It will tell you the time better than the ship's navigator.
sentences.zh: 它报时比船上的领航员更准。

sentences.en: That's what you need.
sentences.zh: 这才是你所需要的。

sentences.en: What followed were over 20 years of working and reworking and re-reworking designs for various Harrison C-clocks.
sentences.zh: 随后的20多年里，他不断地对各种哈里森C系列钟表进行设计、重做和再重做。

sentences.en: All this time, John Harrison had been tinkering and tinkering, making prototypes with changes big and small to the same basic formula as H1.
sentences.zh: 在这段时间里，约翰·哈里森一直在修修补补，制作原型机，对H1的基本公式进行大大小小的改动。

sentences.en: But then, in the mid-1750s, Harrison just happened to get a new pocket watch.
sentences.zh: 但后来，在18世纪50年代中期，哈里森偶然得到了一块新的怀表。

sentences.en: The watch was for his personal use, made by another clockmaker.
sentences.zh: 这块表是他个人使用的，由另一位钟表匠制造。

sentences.en: At the time, watches were extremely unreliable, even more so than regular clocks, which, as we've established, were very crappy.
sentences.zh: 当时，怀表极其不可靠，甚至比普通的钟表还要差，而我们已经确定，那些钟表本身就很烂。

sentences.en: You know, a gentleman might have a pocket watch, but it was just for vanity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，绅士可能会有一块怀表，但那只是为了虚荣。

sentences.en: It didn't really keep good time.
sentences.zh: 它走时并不准。

sentences.en: But this watch, which used some of Harrison's improvements, was extremely accurate.
sentences.zh: 但这块表，由于运用了哈里森的一些改进，变得极其精准。

sentences.en: Harrison looked down at his shiny new pocket watch, and he realized that the key to a perfect C-clock was that he needed to think smaller.
sentences.zh: 哈里森低头看着他那块闪亮的新怀表，意识到制造完美C系列钟表的关键在于他需要把思路缩小。

sentences.en: His other clocks were massive,
sentences.zh: 他其他的钟表都太庞大了，

sentences.en: and wouldn't it be so much better to have something small and practical that a captain out at sea could keep on him at all times and carry in his hand?
sentences.zh: 如果能有一种小巧实用的东西，让船长在海上随时带在身上，拿在手里，那该多好啊？

sentences.en: It took him four years to complete his C-watch, H4.
sentences.zh: 他花了四年时间完成了他的C系列怀表，即H4。

sentences.en: H4 was five inches in diameter, and it weighed just three pounds.
sentences.zh: H4直径五英寸，重量仅为三磅。

sentences.en: So compared to the carry-on luggage of H1, it could fit in a free personal item.
sentences.zh: 所以和H1那种随身行李相比，它甚至可以放进免费的个人物品里。

sentences.en: Except on Spirit Airlines.
sentences.zh: 除了在精神航空上。

sentences.en: Then it would probably cost 50 bucks.
sentences.zh: 那样的话可能要花50美元。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Looking at H4 and the Royal Observatory, I was struck by just how different it looks from any of Harrison's earlier C-clocks.
sentences.zh: 在皇家天文台看着H4，我被它与哈里森早期任何C系列钟表截然不同的外观所震撼。

sentences.en: If the other ones look pretty steampunk, this looks just, like, so ornate and beautiful and delicate.
sentences.zh: 如果说其他的看起来很有蒸汽朋克感，那这个看起来就非常华丽、精美且细腻。

sentences.en: Like, how would you describe that?
sentences.zh: 比如，你会怎么形容它？

sentences.en: There's all this, like, curving filigree, these blue iridescent dots.
sentences.zh: 上面有各种弯曲的细丝工艺，还有蓝色的虹彩圆点。

sentences.en: There's, like, rubies and diamonds in there, right?
sentences.zh: 上面还有红宝石和钻石，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: So diamond pallets, we're still not entirely sure how he made them.
sentences.zh: 所以钻石托盘，我们至今仍不完全确定他是怎么制作出来的。

sentences.en: I was going to say, are the gems just, like, gratuitous?
sentences.zh: 我正想问，这些宝石只是为了装饰吗？

sentences.en: Are they flair?
sentences.zh: 它们是花哨的摆设吗？

sentences.en: Do they have a purpose?
sentences.zh: 它们有实际用途吗？

sentences.en: They have a purpose.
sentences.zh: 它们有用途。

sentences.en: They do, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实有，是的。

sentences.en: And it's all anti-friction or minimizing friction.
sentences.zh: 它们都是为了抗摩擦或最大限度地减少摩擦。

sentences.en: When Harrison finished H4, he didn't do what he'd done with his other inventions.
sentences.zh: 当哈里森完成H4时，他没有像对待其他发明那样做。

sentences.en: He didn't insist that this one wasn't right or ask for more time.
sentences.zh: 他没有坚持说这个还不完美，也没有要求更多时间。

sentences.en: He was finally, finally ready to have his work tested and collect the longitude prize.
sentences.zh: 他终于，终于准备好让他的作品接受测试并领取经度奖金了。

sentences.en: Perfectionist, do you think?
sentences.zh: 完美主义者，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So that's what was one of the most interesting things to me, that when he made H4, he knew he'd really done it.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我来说是最有趣的事情之一，当他制造出H4时，他知道他真的做到了。

sentences.en: And he had this wonderful saying, I think I remember it, it was,
sentences.zh: 他有一句很棒的话，我想我记得，它是，

sentences.en: I think it is fair to say that there is no other mechanical thing that is as beautiful or as curious in texture as this my watch or timekeeper for the longitude.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，没有任何其他机械装置能像我这块用于测定经度的手表或计时器这样，在结构上如此美观或奇妙。

sentences.en: Satisfied, finally, with his invention, Harrison presented H4 to the board of longitude.
sentences.zh: 哈里森终于对自己的发明感到满意，将H4呈交给了经度委员会。

sentences.en: The board agreed to send the timepiece on its official trial to Jamaica, with that big fat pile of quid resting on the results.
sentences.zh: 委员会同意将这台计时器送去牙买加进行正式试航，那一大笔奖金就取决于结果了。

sentences.en: To take top prize, Harrison would need to bring H4 by sea to Jamaica and then, on arrival, take longitude calculations.
sentences.zh: 要获得最高奖金，哈里森需要通过海路将H4带到牙买加，然后在抵达时进行经度计算。

sentences.en: If the difference between Harrison's number and the real longitude of Jamaica was within 30 nautical miles or half a degree of longitude, he would at long last take home the prize.
sentences.zh: 如果哈里森测得的数字与牙买加的真实经度之差在30海里或半个经度以内，他最终就能把奖金带回家。

sentences.en: Harrison himself was getting up in age.
sentences.zh: 哈里森本人年纪也大了。

sentences.en: He was almost 70.
sentences.zh: 他快70岁了。

sentences.en: So in classic dad fashion, he made his kid do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，典型的老爸作风，他让他儿子去干这事。

sentences.en: In 1761, Harrison's son, William, traveled with H4 all the way across the Atlantic Ocean on a two-month journey through icy cold, humid heat and rolling seas.
sentences.zh: 1761年，哈里森的儿子威廉带着H4横跨大西洋，经历了两个月的旅程，穿过了冰冷、潮湿和波涛汹涌的海面。

sentences.en: He collected his data, which was accurate to about a single nautical mile, way closer than the 30-mile cutoff.
sentences.zh: 他收集的数据非常准确，误差仅在一海里左右，远超30海里的及格线。

sentences.en: But when William returned home expecting to claim the reward, the board of longitude said that, sorry, actually, the trial was void,
sentences.zh: 但当威廉回到家准备领取奖金时，经度委员会却说，抱歉，实际上这次试航无效，

sentences.en: partly because they thought the result might be a fluke, and partly because they didn't actually know the longitude of Jamaica.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他们认为结果可能是侥幸，部分原因是他们实际上根本不知道牙买加的经度。

sentences.en: They sent him to Jamaica, even though they weren't sure where Jamaica was.
sentences.zh: 他们把他派往牙买加，尽管他们自己都不确定牙买加在哪里。

sentences.en: This was insane behavior, a huge waste of time.
sentences.zh: 这简直是疯狂的行为，纯粹是浪费时间。

sentences.en: Obviously, the Harrisons were exasperated.
sentences.zh: 显然，哈里森一家被激怒了。

sentences.en: From this point on, the board of longitude kept holding the prize just out of reach.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，经度委员会一直把奖金悬在半空中，让他够不着。

sentences.en: In 1764, Harrison got a new trial, this time to Barbados.
sentences.zh: 1764年，哈里森获得了新的试航机会，这次是去巴巴多斯。

sentences.en: He aces it again, but the board equivocates.
sentences.zh: 他再次大获全胜，但委员会却含糊其辞。

sentences.en: They kept moving the goalpoSt.
sentences.zh: 他们不断地改变规则。

sentences.en: Harrison may have finally perfected his watch, but his timing was horrible.
sentences.zh: 哈里森可能终于完善了他的手表，但他的时机太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It took him so long that by this point, most of his friends and allies on the board had retired or just straight up died.
sentences.zh: 他花了太长时间，以至于此时，委员会中他大多数的朋友和盟友都已经退休或直接去世了。

sentences.en: And the new commissioners of longitude were unfortunately the worst thing an eccentric creative type could encounter.
sentences.zh: 而新的经度专员不幸地成了古怪创意型人才最不想遇到的人。

sentences.en: They were pragmatists.
sentences.zh: 他们是实用主义者。

sentences.en: Here's Alexi Baker again.
sentences.zh: 这是亚历克西·贝克再次登场。

sentences.en: The big problem, the reason he was conflicting with the commissioners, is they thought it wouldn't help the nation if they couldn't also replicate his watches.
sentences.zh: 最大的问题，他与专员们产生冲突的原因是，他们认为如果不能复制他的手表，这对国家就没有帮助。

sentences.en: The board of longitude was looking at Harrison and saying, this is a guy who's over 70 years old.
sentences.zh: 经度委员会看着哈里森说，这家伙已经70多岁了。

sentences.en: He'd taken decades to build one watch, and they weren't even sure he could make a second one,
sentences.zh: 他花了数十年才造出一块表，而且他们甚至不确定他能否造出第二块，

sentences.en: let alone put them in the hands of every captain trying to make their way across the open seas.
sentences.zh: 更不用说让每一位试图横渡大洋的船长都能用上它了。

sentences.en: So they could be amazing one-offs, but would it be affordable and possible for other people, because he was getting on in age, for other people to make a lot more watches?
sentences.zh: 所以，这些表或许能成为令人惊叹的孤品，但考虑到他年事已高，让其他人也能大量制造这些表，这在经济上和现实中可行吗？

sentences.en: Not to mention that Harrison had in fact been so slow that the astronomers who had taken centuries to find a solution to longitude had basically caught up.
sentences.zh: 更别提哈里森的进度实在太慢，以至于那些花了几个世纪寻找经度解决方案的天文学家们基本上已经追上来了。

sentences.en: They actually had found an okay way of calculating longitude called the lunar distance method.
sentences.zh: 他们确实找到了一种计算经度的可行方法，叫做月距法。

sentences.en: And it worked.
sentences.zh: 而且它奏效了。

sentences.en: As long as you had a highly educated person on board, a set of tables, and several hours of calculation time to spare.
sentences.zh: 前提是你船上得有一位受过高等教育的人，一套表格，以及几个小时的空闲计算时间。

sentences.en: The board of longitude kept setting up new hoops for Harrison to jump through.
sentences.zh: 经度委员会不断给哈里森设置新的障碍。

sentences.en: Harrison lost his patience, and he and his son, William, started publishing attacks against the board.
sentences.zh: 哈里森失去了耐心，他和儿子威廉开始公开发表文章抨击委员会。

sentences.en: I honestly, even though it's silly to feel sorry for people in the 1700s, I feel sorry for both the Harrisons and the commissioners, because they both had very valid points.
sentences.zh: 老实说，尽管为18世纪的人感到难过显得很傻，但我确实同时同情哈里森父子和那些委员们，因为他们双方都有非常正当的理由。

sentences.en: And also, you can definitely understand John Harrison was old by the standards of the time.
sentences.zh: 而且，你绝对可以理解，以当时的眼光来看，约翰·哈里森已经老了。

sentences.en: He was tired.
sentences.zh: 他累了。

sentences.en: He had more medical ailments.
sentences.zh: 他还有不少健康问题。

sentences.en: He wanted this solved and to get his reward, you know.
sentences.zh: 他只想解决这个问题并拿到他的奖金，你知道的。

sentences.en: He just wants to be done with this f***ing clock.
sentences.zh: 他只是想搞定这该死的钟表，然后一了百了。

sentences.en: Yes, it had been his whole life.
sentences.zh: 是的，这已经成了他的一生。

sentences.en: Since 1730s.
sentences.zh: 从1730年代开始。

sentences.en: In the end, Harrison and his son decided to pull the boldest, most daring card they had up their sleeve.
sentences.zh: 最终，哈里森和他的儿子决定使出他们手中最大胆、最冒险的一招。

sentences.en: They tattled.
sentences.zh: 他们去告状了。

sentences.en: William Harrison personally appealed to famous clock enthusiast and America loser King George III to step in.
sentences.zh: 威廉·哈里森亲自向著名的钟表爱好者、美国的“失败者”乔治三世国王求助，希望他能介入。

sentences.en: There were many reasons to cry, this is unfair,
sentences.zh: 有很多理由让人哭诉这不公平，

sentences.en: and the king agreed that it was unfair and tested the fifth one in his private observatory and was convinced that Harrison had been very, very badly treated.
sentences.zh: 国王也认为这不公平，并在他的私人天文台测试了第五台钟表，确信哈里森受到了非常、非常糟糕的对待。

sentences.en: Speaking to William at Windsor Castle, the king supposedly said that they had been cruelly treated and exclaimed, by God, Harrison, I will see you righted.
sentences.zh: 据称，国王在温莎城堡对威廉说，他们受到了残酷的对待，并大喊道：“看在上帝的份上，哈里森，我会为你主持公道的。”

sentences.en: In 1772, King George tested a copy of H4 called, you guessed it, H5, and was thoroughly impressed by its accuracy.
sentences.zh: 1772年，乔治国王测试了H4的一个复制品，也就是你猜到的，H5，并对其精准度留下了深刻印象。

sentences.en: At the instruction of the king, Parliament awarded John Harrison the rest of the money he was owed as a thank you for his decades of work.
sentences.zh: 在国王的指示下，议会授予了约翰·哈里森他应得的剩余奖金，作为对他数十年工作的感谢。

sentences.en: Crucially, though, the money was only a thank you.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，这笔钱仅仅是感谢金。

sentences.en: It was not the longitude prize, which the board maintained he had not earned.
sentences.zh: 它并不是经度奖金，委员会坚持认为他并没有赢得那笔奖金。

sentences.en: Of course he felt hard done by.
sentences.zh: 当然，他觉得自己受到了不公正的待遇。

sentences.en: He was probably never fully happy, even after he got that recognition.
sentences.zh: 即使在获得认可之后，他可能也从未真正感到完全快乐。

sentences.en: Harrison died in 1776, just a few years later.
sentences.zh: 哈里森于1776年去世，仅仅几年之后。

sentences.en: And it did take a minute, or more like a few decades, for manufacturers to even come close to replicating the near perfection of H4.
sentences.zh: 确实花了一段时间，或者说几十年，制造商们才接近复制出H4那种近乎完美的水平。

sentences.en: But by the early 19th century, variations of Harrison's sea watch were everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但到了19世纪初，哈里森航海钟的各种变体已经随处可见。

sentences.en: These instruments became generically known as marine chronometers.
sentences.zh: 这些仪器被统称为航海天文钟。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, the marine chronometer did exactly what Parliament had hoped when they first set up the Longitude Act over a century earlier.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，航海天文钟的作用恰恰实现了议会在一个多世纪前制定《经度法案》时的初衷。

sentences.en: It threw gasoline on the fire of British imperialism.
sentences.zh: 它为大英帝国的扩张火上浇油。

sentences.en: The Royal Navy made marine chronometers standard issue.
sentences.zh: 英国皇家海军将航海天文钟列为标准配置。

sentences.en: And captains of merchant vessels, like those sailing with the British East India Company, got their own chronometers too.
sentences.zh: 而像那些随英国东印度公司航行的商船船长们，也拥有了自己的天文钟。

sentences.en: Here's Deva Sobel again.
sentences.zh: 再次请出戴娃·索贝尔。

sentences.en: Once they really knew where they were going and where they were, that was a powerful aid to many things they did, for good and ill.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们真正知道自己要去哪里以及身在何处，这对他们所做的一切都是强有力的辅助，无论好坏。

sentences.en: By the time marine chronometers were widespread, Britain had abolished slavery and left the transatlantic slave trade.
sentences.zh: 当航海天文钟普及之时，英国已经废除了奴隶制并退出了跨大西洋奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: But it was colonizing faster than ever, spreading beyond North America and the Caribbean and into Africa, Asia, and the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 但它的殖民扩张比以往任何时候都快，从北美和加勒比地区蔓延到了非洲、亚洲和太平洋地区。

sentences.en: And since any tool that helped navigation helped imperialism, the marine chronometer was a key part of the evil doings.
sentences.zh: 既然任何有助于航海的工具都有助于帝国主义，那么航海天文钟就是这些罪恶行径的关键部分。

sentences.en: In the end, the marine chronometer ended up being just one tool in a toolbox full of tools that the British used for world domination.
sentences.zh: 最终，航海天文钟成了英国用于称霸世界的工具箱里的一件工具。

sentences.en: But actually, one of the chronometer's most lasting impacts came indirectly, from its role in mapmaking.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，天文钟最持久的影响之一是间接产生的，源于它在地图绘制中的作用。

sentences.en: James Cook used his Harrison-style chronometer on his second voyage.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·库克在第二次航行中使用了他的哈里森式天文钟。

sentences.en: He took it south of the Antarctic Circle, where he surveyed parts of the world never before represented on European maps.
sentences.zh: 他带着它深入南极圈以南，勘测了欧洲地图上从未出现过的地区。

sentences.en: And the logbooks on his ship, the HMS Resolution, called the chronometer, our trusty friend, the watch.
sentences.zh: 他的船“决心号”上的航海日志将这台天文钟称为“我们值得信赖的朋友，那块表”。

sentences.en: In 1831, the surveying vessel, the HMS Beagle, carried Charles Darwin to the Galapagos.
sentences.zh: 1831年，勘测船“小猎犬号”载着查尔斯·达尔文前往加拉帕戈斯群岛。

sentences.en: It also carried 22 marine chronometers.
sentences.zh: 船上还携带了22台航海天文钟。

sentences.en: You know, just in case.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，以防万一。

sentences.en: Bare minimum, you'd have a few, because you would use them all and then compare them.
sentences.zh: 最起码你也得带几台，因为你会把它们都用上，然后进行比对。

sentences.en: You want to have backup.
sentences.zh: 你需要备份。

sentences.en: You always want to have backup.
sentences.zh: 你总是需要备份。

sentences.en: The widespread use of marine chronometers meant that by the late 19th century,
sentences.zh: 航海天文钟的广泛使用意味着到了19世纪末，

sentences.en: most Western trading vessels were using British maritime charts.
sentences.zh: 大多数西方商船都在使用英国的海图。

sentences.en: So when a global conference was held to pick one standard line of zero degrees longitude for the international community,
sentences.zh: 因此，当全球会议召开以选定一条标准的零度经线供国际社会使用时，

sentences.en: the choice was obvious.
sentences.zh: 选择显而易见。

sentences.en: Greenwich, England was chosen as Longitude Zero, the prime meridian.
sentences.zh: 英国格林威治被选为零度经线，即本初子午线。

sentences.en: And with that, England, with the help of John Harrison, became, cartographically speaking, the center of the world.
sentences.zh: 至此，在约翰·哈里森的帮助下，英国在地图学上成为了世界的中心。

sentences.en: I wonder how having longitude changed navigation.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇拥有经度是如何改变航海的。

sentences.en: People stopped dying so much.
sentences.zh: 人们不再那么容易丧命了。

sentences.en: Back on the Buccaneer with Todd, as he was steering us through jagged rocks and hundreds of shipwrecks,
sentences.zh: 回到托德的“海盗号”上，当他驾驶着我们穿过锯齿状的岩石和数百处沉船点时，

sentences.en: I didn't take for granted that I could just look at the dashboard and get information
sentences.zh: 我并没有把能直接看仪表盘获取信息视为理所当然，

sentences.en: that a few hundred years ago would have seemed like a miracle.
sentences.zh: 这在几百年前看来简直是奇迹。

sentences.en: You're looking at the screen right now.
sentences.zh: 你现在正看着屏幕。

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: That's the GPS.
sentences.zh: 那是GPS。

sentences.en: It shows you where all the rocks are and where all the wrecks are.
sentences.zh: 它显示了所有岩石和沉船的位置。

sentences.en: I'll put them on there.
sentences.zh: 我会把它们标在上面。

sentences.en: And what's our longitude right now?
sentences.zh: 那么我们现在的经度是多少？

sentences.en: Our longitude, we're north 4953-340, west 006-21-368.
sentences.zh: 我们的经度是北纬49度53分340秒，西经0度6分21秒368毫秒。

sentences.en: Good to know.
sentences.zh: 知道了。

sentences.en: After the break, we talk about a method for long-distance sea travel that existed millennia before Europeans cracked longitude.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我们将讨论一种在欧洲人破解经度难题前就已经存在了数千年的远洋航行方法。

sentences.en: So I'm back with Kelly Prime.
sentences.zh: 我又回到了凯利·普莱姆身边。

sentences.en: I hear you have some more for me.
sentences.zh: 听说你还有更多内容要告诉我。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So as I was reporting this story, one element kept coming up for me,
sentences.zh: 在我报道这个故事时，有一个要素一直浮现在我脑海中，

sentences.en: which is that the story we're telling about longitude and the longitude problem and the act is a very Eurocentric one.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们讲述的关于经度、经度问题和法案的故事，是一个非常欧洲中心主义的故事。

sentences.en: Like, yeah, I can't, like, actually picture any of these characters not wearing powdered legs, you know?
sentences.zh: 就像，是的，我无法想象这些角色中哪一个是不戴假发的，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: That's totally true.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是真的。

sentences.en: And since the problem of finding longitude was essentially the problem of figuring out a way to safely travel long distances at sea,
sentences.zh: 既然寻找经度的问题本质上是如何安全地进行远距离海上航行的问题，

sentences.en: I was really curious about how other cultures managed to do that.
sentences.zh: 我真的很好奇其他文化是如何做到这一点的。

sentences.en: And the most extraordinary version that I found comes from the Pacific Islands, where navigators have been traveling between these, like, teensy,
sentences.zh: 我发现的最非凡的版本来自太平洋岛屿，那里的航海家们几千年来一直在这些，比如，极小的、

sentences.en: tiny islands separated by thousands of miles of ocean for millennia, like, centuries and centuries before the Longitude Act.
sentences.zh: 被数千英里海洋隔开的岛屿之间穿梭，比《经度法案》早了几个世纪。

sentences.en: So to find out more, I called up probably, like, one of the coolest people I've ever met.
sentences.zh: 所以为了了解更多，我联系了可能是我见过最酷的人之一。

sentences.en: My name is Lehua Kamalu, and I am a captain and navigator and sometimes crew member of traditional Polynesian voyaging canoes.
sentences.zh: 我叫莱胡阿·卡马鲁，我是传统波利尼西亚航海独木舟的船长、航海家，有时也是船员。

sentences.en: Lehua Kamalu is based in Honolulu and works on the canoes Hokulea and Hikianalia.
sentences.zh: 莱胡阿·卡马鲁常驻檀香山，在“霍库雷亚号”和“希基阿纳利亚号”独木舟上工作。

sentences.en: And she's one of the few people on Earth using traditional skills to navigate vast distances at sea, which means no GPS and definitely no marine chronometer.
sentences.zh: 她是地球上为数不多利用传统技能在海上进行远距离航行的人之一，这意味着没有GPS，也绝对没有航海天文钟。

sentences.en: There is no timepiece involved in the wayfinding in this way, and so I'll probably call it non-instrument navigation.
sentences.zh: 这种寻路方式不涉及任何计时器，所以我可能会称之为“无仪器导航”。

sentences.en: That's probably the simplest way to describe it.
sentences.zh: 这可能是最简单的描述方式。

sentences.en: I mean, to me, there's nothing simple about navigating thousands of miles between tiny islands in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对我而言，在太平洋中部的小岛之间航行数千英里，一点也不简单。

sentences.en: But so how does she do it?
sentences.zh: 那么她是怎么做到的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I'll say first that a lot of the original techniques for this kind of navigation have been lost over the years because of colonization.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先我要说，这种导航的许多原始技术因为殖民化而在多年间失传了。

sentences.en: But Lehua and her colleagues use their own interpretation of the methods that Pacific Islanders use thousands of years ago.
sentences.zh: 但莱胡阿和她的同事们运用了他们自己对太平洋岛民数千年前所用方法的解读。

sentences.en: Back then, navigators in the Pacific Islands had a lot of the same challenges as Europeans.
sentences.zh: 那时，太平洋岛屿的航海家们面临着与欧洲人相同的许多挑战。

sentences.en: Basically, there's only so much information you can easily get from the sun and the stars.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你能从太阳和星星中轻松获取的信息是有限的。

sentences.en: And so it kind of makes sense that the starting point for Polynesian wayfinding is actually pretty similar to the European concept of dead reckoning.
sentences.zh: 所以波利尼西亚寻路法的出发点与欧洲的推测航法概念非常相似，这也就说得通了。

sentences.en: You need to constantly be watching.
sentences.zh: 你需要时刻保持观察。

sentences.en: Like, are we making good progress?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们进展顺利吗？

sentences.en: Are we still doing the same speed?
sentences.zh: 我们还在保持同样的速度吗？

sentences.en: Are we a little slower?
sentences.zh: 我们慢了一点吗？

sentences.en: Are we a little faster?
sentences.zh: 我们快了一点吗？

sentences.en: You know, are these conditions the standard conditions that we expect?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些状况是我们预期的标准状况吗？

sentences.en: Or are we experiencing something that is out of the norm?
sentences.zh: 还是我们遇到了不同寻常的情况？

sentences.en: And how do we account for that?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何应对？

sentences.en: Ultimately, though, this approach isn't enough.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这种方法是不够的。

sentences.en: Lehua says it gets you in the right direction, but the longer the journey, the more errors can add up.
sentences.zh: 莱胡阿说，它能让你保持正确的方向，但航程越长，累积的误差就越多。

sentences.en: So you need a way to get more confident in where you are and where you're going at sea.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要一种方法来更确定你在海上所处的位置和航向。

sentences.en: And so instead of using something like latitude and longitude, Polynesian wayfinders take a more holistic approach.
sentences.zh: 因此，波利尼西亚寻路者没有使用纬度和经度之类的东西，而是采取了一种更整体的方法。

sentences.en: Let's just imagine the world, not so much with an imaginary grid on it, and rather just see it in the natural way that it is.
sentences.zh: 让我们想象一下这个世界，不要把它看作是一个带有虚构网格的平面，而是以它本来的自然方式去看待它。

sentences.en: And I think what it forces you to do is to allow nature to tell you where you are and not you to tell nature where you are.
sentences.zh: 我认为这强迫你做的是让大自然告诉你你在哪里，而不是你告诉大自然你在哪里。

sentences.en: And what does that mean exactly, letting nature tell you where you are?
sentences.zh: 那么“让大自然告诉你你在哪里”到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Okay, so what Lehua told me is that even when you're out at sea, way out of sight of land, that doesn't mean you don't have information.
sentences.zh: 好的，莱胡阿告诉我，即使你在海上，远离陆地，那也不意味着你没有信息。

sentences.en: In fact, your natural surroundings provide a lot of data that can be used to figure out where you are and where you're going.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你的自然环境提供了大量数据，可以用来判断你在哪里以及要去哪里。

sentences.en: It's not that you are traveling from point A to point B with absolutely nothing in the middle.
sentences.zh: 并不是说你从A点到B点，中间什么都没有。

sentences.en: There is an ocean that is pointing you in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 有一片海洋在为你指引正确的方向。

sentences.en: There are wave patterns.
sentences.zh: 有波浪模式。

sentences.en: There are animals.
sentences.zh: 有动物。

sentences.en: There are wind directions.
sentences.zh: 有风向。

sentences.en: There are clouds in the sky.
sentences.zh: 天上有云。

sentences.en: There is a never-ending display of celestial bodies,
sentences.zh: 有永无止境的天体展示，

sentences.en: of planets and stars and the sun and the moon and all these features that are continuously telling you what direction you're going in if you're paying attention.
sentences.zh: 行星、恒星、太阳、月亮以及所有这些特征，如果你留心观察，它们会不断告诉你你正朝着什么方向前进。

sentences.en: So I think I understand that there are these natural features in the environment that you can use to navigate.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我明白了，环境中有这些可以用来导航的自然特征。

sentences.en: But how does she apply what she's seeing and hearing?
sentences.zh: 但她是如何应用她所看到和听到的呢？

sentences.en: Like how does she make practical sense of it all in terms of setting a specific course for her canoe?
sentences.zh: 比如，她是如何在为独木舟设定特定航线时，将这一切转化为实际意义的？

sentences.en: Great question.
sentences.zh: 好问题。

sentences.en: And one example that LaHua gave me was birds, specifically land birds.
sentences.zh: 莱胡阿给我的一个例子是鸟类，特别是陆地鸟类。

sentences.en: So you might be trying to locate one little island in the Pacific and you could be out of sight of land.
sentences.zh: 你可能正试图在太平洋中定位一个小岛，而你可能正处于看不见陆地的位置。

sentences.en: But if you look up and see a land bird flying overhead, like a type of bird that you know doesn't like to go very far from home, that tells you something.
sentences.zh: 但如果你抬头看到一只陆地鸟飞过，比如那种你知道不喜欢离家太远的鸟，那就会告诉你一些信息。

sentences.en: And it means you're in the radius of some kind of land.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你处于某种陆地的半径范围内。

sentences.en: And suddenly you see that island, if you imagine the island not just as the land above the water, but also the animals and the birds that live on that island,
sentences.zh: 突然间你看到了那个岛，如果你把岛屿想象成不仅仅是水面之上的陆地，还包括生活在岛上的动物和鸟类，

sentences.en: they are part of that island as well.
sentences.zh: 它们也是岛屿的一部分。

sentences.en: So the island becomes much bigger.
sentences.zh: 所以岛屿变得大得多了。

sentences.en: And soon you start to say, well, also the waves around that island are affected much further out.
sentences.zh: 很快你就会说，嗯，岛屿周围的波浪也会受到更远范围的影响。

sentences.en: So in a way, those waves are also part of that island.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，那些波浪也是岛屿的一部分。

sentences.en: And suddenly the island is actually just this massive target.
sentences.zh: 突然间，这个岛实际上成了一个巨大的目标。

sentences.en: And if you start to see all the signs that say, I'm an island, it's not just land, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你开始看到所有写着“我是一个岛”的迹象，那不仅仅是陆地，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't just have to see a rock or a tree to know an island is there.
sentences.zh: 你不需要非得看到岩石或树木才知道岛屿就在那里。

sentences.en: And I think that suddenly makes you realize how going after one island that might only be 10 miles around becomes going after an island that's 200 or 300 miles around.
sentences.zh: 我认为这让你突然意识到，去寻找一个可能只有10英里周长的岛屿，变成了去寻找一个200或300英里周长的岛屿。

sentences.en: And you're trying to expand your perspective to see the ways that you can see an island without actually just seeing the island itself.
sentences.zh: 你正在尝试扩展你的视角，去寻找那些无需亲眼看到岛屿本身就能发现它的方式。

sentences.en: I love this so much.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: It's so cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, OK, so, you know, she can see a 10 mile island as a 300 mile island.
sentences.zh: 所以，好的，你知道，她能把一个10英里的岛看作一个300英里的岛。

sentences.en: And that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: And but I do wonder, like, as, you know, you are relying on the natural world to be your sort of navigational guide, that climate changes and changes in the environment, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我确实想知道，当你依赖自然世界作为你的导航指南时，气候变化和环境变化，你知道，

sentences.en: like could change the way she should read them.
sentences.zh: 是否会改变她解读这些信号的方式？

sentences.en: Did she talk about that?
sentences.zh: 她谈到过这一点吗？

sentences.en: She did, because, you know, like you're saying, when the entire basis of your navigation system is the natural world,
sentences.zh: 她谈到了，因为，你知道，就像你说的，当你的导航系统的整个基础是自然世界时，

sentences.en: even like the tiniest changes to one ocean current or one species of bird can make a massive difference.
sentences.zh: 即使是洋流或鸟类物种的微小变化，也可能产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: I think it's really something I think about a lot today is just how much life in the ocean is no longer there.
sentences.zh: 我想这确实是我今天经常思考的问题，那就是海洋中已经消失了多少生命。

sentences.en: When you think about how critical just that one bird is, you start to connect all of the sensitivities of the system and it all has to work for it to work for you.
sentences.zh: 当你想到仅仅那一种鸟类有多关键时，你就会开始将系统中所有的敏感因素联系起来，而这一切必须环环相扣，才能为你所用。

sentences.en: So you become quite attentive to what supports the system that allows the navigation.
sentences.zh: 所以你会变得非常关注那些支持导航系统的因素。

sentences.en: And that is a healthy ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 那就是一个健康的生态系统。

sentences.en: I mean, you think about one species of bird that lives on an island and if something happened to that one species, she would know the difference,
sentences.zh: 我是说，你试想一下，如果某种生活在岛上的鸟类物种发生了什么意外，她会察觉到其中的差异，

sentences.en: like it would affect her navigation potentially.
sentences.zh: 比如这可能会影响她的导航。

sentences.en: It's just sort of an amazing concept to sort of think about.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个令人惊叹的概念，值得深思。

sentences.en: Yeah, she actually talked about feral cat colonies on islands and how when there's feral cat colonies, those cats will kill the birds.
sentences.zh: 没错，她实际上谈到了岛上的野猫群，以及当有野猫群存在时，这些猫会捕杀鸟类。

sentences.en: And when you don't have the birds, you don't have the birds at sea.
sentences.zh: 而当你没有了这些鸟，你在海上也就失去了它们。

sentences.en: So it's like even one tiny, tiny thing throws off how you can find where you are in the ocean.
sentences.zh: 所以，哪怕是一件微不足道的小事，都会打乱你在海洋中定位的能力。

sentences.en: It's kind of crazy.
sentences.zh: 这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: It is crazy.
sentences.zh: 确实很疯狂。

sentences.en: It's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: So I also want to mention that L'Hua and her colleagues at the Polynesian Voyaging Society are currently doing this big project to circumnavigate the Pacific on traditional voyaging canoes.
sentences.zh: 我还想提一下，L'Hua 和她在波利尼西亚航海协会的同事们目前正在进行一个大型项目，驾驶传统的航海独木舟环游太平洋。

sentences.en: It's a 43,000 nautical mile voyage.
sentences.zh: 这是一次 43,000 海里的航行。

sentences.en: And L'Hua is one of 400 crew members taking turns doing different legs of this journey.
sentences.zh: L'Hua 是 400 名船员之一，他们轮流完成这段旅程的不同航段。

sentences.en: And the day I talked to L'Hua, she was getting ready.
sentences.zh: 我采访 L'Hua 的那天，她正在做准备。

sentences.en: It was literally the day before.
sentences.zh: 那真的是在出发前一天。

sentences.en: She was getting ready to fly out to start a 2,000 mile journey from the Cook Islands to New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 她正准备飞往库克群岛，开启一段 2,000 英里的航程，前往新西兰。

sentences.en: And the whole voyage should take about four years.
sentences.zh: 整个航行大约需要四年时间。

sentences.en: I think they started in 2023.
sentences.zh: 我想他们是在 2023 年出发的。

sentences.en: Wait, and she was getting on the phone to talk to you the day before she was leaving on this four-year journey?
sentences.zh: 等等，她是在出发进行这四年旅程的前一天，还在电话里和你聊天？

sentences.en: Yeah, she was like, I should really, really pack.
sentences.zh: 是的，她当时说，我真的真的该去打包了。

sentences.en: I should really pack.
sentences.zh: 我真的该去打包了。

sentences.en: But this wasn't, you know, she's doing one leg of the journey.
sentences.zh: 但这不是，你知道的，她只是负责其中一个航段。

sentences.en: She was going to do one leg.
sentences.zh: 她只打算完成一个航段。

sentences.en: Okay, that sounds better.
sentences.zh: 好的，那听起来合理多了。

sentences.en: Okay, that sounds good.
sentences.zh: 好的，那听起来不错。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the whole voyage should take four years.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以整个航行应该需要四年。

sentences.en: And the goal is to connect communities in the Pacific and also to spread awareness about the importance of protecting indigenous knowledge and ocean ecosysteMs.
sentences.zh: 其目标是连接太平洋地区的各个社区，并传播保护本土知识和海洋生态系统重要性的意识。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: So is there a way to track where she is in the world?
sentences.zh: 那么有什么办法可以追踪她在世界上的位置吗？

sentences.en: There is, yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的，可以。

sentences.en: Yeah, so you can go to the Polynesian Voyaging Society website, and there's a map that lets you track the journey, the various legs of the journey.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以访问波利尼西亚航海协会的网站，上面有一张地图，可以让你追踪这段旅程以及各个航段。

sentences.en: That is so cool.
sentences.zh: 那太酷了。

sentences.en: I'm so glad we talked about this.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们聊了这个话题。

sentences.en: This is so much fun.
sentences.zh: 这太有意思了。
